stem: Describe how division of labour leads to specialisation. Support your answer with examples from the extract.
context: In 2019 thatch grass vendors in the Kavango region of Namibia used division of labour to specialise in the harvesting, bundle-making and selling of thatch grass as their main source of income.  Due to an increase in tourism and construction of lodges, the sales of thatch grass in Namibia have increased and contributed hugely to the household income of rural people.  Although the demand for the grass outstripped the supply of the grass, the vendors were not able to increase the supply of thatch grass, due to not having advanced harvesting machinery and tools.  Since the thatch grass market was not regulated, buyers could decide on the price that they were willing to pay per bundle.  The buyers then sold the grass at much higher prices to businesses such as lodges and hotels.  These were some of the biggest markets that used the thatch grass for roofs.  In 2020, due to the six-month long Covid-19 imposed state of emergency, the tourism and construction industries in Namibia were affected very badly and the vendors of thatch grass faced possible closure as there was no market for their product. (Adapted article from The Namibian, 13 October 2020)

stem: Explain the form of business organisation of the berry farming business.
context: In July 2020, a local private limited Namibian company, harvested Namibia’s first-ever commercial blueberries which are cultivated next to the Okavango river.  The Government Institutions Pension Fund (GIPF) has invested N$90 million in this project.  The chairman of the fund said the pensioners’ money was safe, because of the good returns expected from this project.  The quality of the fruit, harvested and marketed under the Namib Blue brand name, has been exceptional and Namibia exported tons of blueberries to, for example, the Netherlands, Germany, Spain, Russia and even Hong Kong. The product is also stocked on local retail shelves. The company was planning to double its production area by the end of 2021 in order to expand its operations.  Blueberries are hand-harvested to ensure that the fruit is not damaged or bruised.  The industry offers employment opportunities to seasonal workers, because during peak harvest times, a larger number of workers is required.  The management of the firm is convinced that, with the right planning, proper infrastructure and efficient management in place, the increasing output might continue to contribute to a fall in average cost.
